([[Tilton, New Hampshire]]) | college = [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] (2015–2019) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = }} '''Terance Mann''' (born October 18, 1996) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]]. ==Early life and high school== Mann was born in [[Brooklyn, New York]] but grew up in [[Lowell, Massachusetts]].{{cite news |last1=Langone |first1=Matt |title=Lowell native Mann stars for Florida State |url=http://www.lowellsun.com/sports/ci_31438622/soaring-seminole |accessdate=April 4, 2019 |work=[[Lowell Sun]]}} Mann is the son of [[Daynia La-Force]], who coaches women's basketball at [[Rhode Island Rams women's basketball|Rhode Island]].{{cite news |last1=Deen |first1=Safid |title=FSU forward Terance Mann credits mother for turning him into strong leader, floor coach |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/florida-state-seminoles/chopping-block/os-sp-fsu-terance-mann-1112-story.html |accessdate=April 4, 2019 |work=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |date=November 11, 2017}} He played for the [[Tilton School]] in New Hampshire. At Tilton School, he averaged 23.1 points and 7.8 rebounds per game as a senior. He led the school to a 31-5 record and the New England Preparatory School Athletic Conference Class AA championship. Mann was a First Team All-NEPSAC selection.{{cite news |title=New Hampshire Boys Basketball POY: Terance Mann |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/gatorade-new-hampshire-boys-basketball-poy-terance-mann |accessdate=April 4, 2019 |work=[[USA Today]] |date=March 20, 2015}} Mann was a four-star recruit and signed with Florida State, turning down offers from [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]], [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]], [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] and [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]] ==College career== As a freshman, Mann averaged 5.2 points and 17 minutes per game playing behind [[Malik Beasley]] and [[Dwayne Bacon]]. He was named a captain as a sophomore and posted 8.4 points and 4.5 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Weiler |first1=Curt |title=The evolution of Florida State 'stat stuffer' Terance Mann |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/football/2019/03/04/terance-mann-florida-state-fsu-mens-basketball-senior-day-leonard-hamilton-charlton-young-seminoles/3056238002/ |accessdate=April 4, 2019 |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |date=March 4, 2019}} Mann came down with a torn abdominal and groin muscle in the first round of the 2017 NCAA Tournament and was limited as the Seminoles reached the Elite Eight.{{cite news |last1=Holton |first1=Brooks |title=Terance Mann: 3 things to know about Florida State basketball's senior guard |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2018/12/01/terance-mann-fsu-florida-state-seminoles-mens-basketball-facts-know/2160698002/ |accessdate=April 4, 2019 |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |date=December 6, 2018}} Mann posted 12.6 points, 5.4 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game as a junior.{{cite news |last1=Keel |first1=Fletcher |title=Fans: Mann most likely to get drafted in 2019 NBA Draft |url=https://www.wctv.tv/content/news/FAN-OPINION-Mann-most-likely-to-get-drafted-in-2019-NBA-Draft-486896001.html |accessdate=April 4, 2019 |work=WCTV |date=June 28, 2018}} As a senior, Mann averaged 11.4 points and 6.5 rebounds per game. He led the team to a 29-8 record and the Sweet Sixteen of the NCAA Tournament.{{cite news |last1=McGahee |first1=Wayne |title=What will Florida State men's basketball look like next season? |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2019/03/29/florida-state-fsu-mens-basketball-2019-2020-preview-mfiondu-kabengele-trent-forrest-leonard-hamilton/3309603002/ |accessdate=April 4, 2019 |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |date=March 29, 2019}} He finished his career as the third player in school history with over 1,200 points, 600 rebounds, 200 assists and 100 steals. == References == {{Reflist}} == External links == *[https://seminoles.com/sports/basketball/roster/terance-mann/ Florida State Seminoles bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Mann, Terance}} [[Category:1996 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Massachusetts]] [[Category:Florida State Seminoles men's basketball players]] [[Category:Small forwards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Brooklyn]]
